 A TDS: COLLABORATION 
 The House of Bernarda Alba 
 November 14–15 and 18–21
 By Federico García Lorca
 In a New Translation by Caridad Svich
 Directed by Emily Mendelsohn 
 Lorca’s seminal play The House of Bernarda Alba follows a family of five daughters in rural Spain locked into mourning for eight years after the death of their father. Their constrained world explodes as the oldest and wealthiest daughter gets engaged to the man the youngest daughters long for. Written in the midst of rising fascism, the play allegorically explores the human cost of a world where image is tightly controlled to suit the needs of power. Through the poetry and music of his language, which Caridad Svich’s translation elegantly preserves, Lorca offers a freedom we can feel. His play is both tragedy and love letter to the wild human spirit, an encouragement for the heart’s opening to “the irresistible beauty of all things.”
